parsed.rationale: All four records are production code (no restraint markers), but the cluster signal here is 'name-collisions', not structural duplication. The canonical definition lives in 'Shared/Playback/Sources/PlaybackCore/PlaybackReason.swift' (package: Playback) as a type-alias-object, while the remaining three records are extensions in separate packages — 'PlayerHeaderView' (PlaybackReason+PlayerHeaderView.swift) and 'app:iOS' (PlaybackReason+App.swift) — each adding package-specific behaviour to the same type. This is the idiomatic Swift pattern of extending a core type at the boundary of each consuming module; the name collision is intentional and load-bearing, not accidental duplication. No consolidation is warranted because collapsing the extensions into the core Playback package would introduce inappropriate upward dependencies on UI (PlayerHeaderView) and app-layer (app:iOS) concerns.
